title: AI teammates inside Microsoft Teams and team chat
subtitle: A colleague people can call, interrupt and invite to meetings, under an identity the organisation governs

stats.label: Teams media soak from Azure to my own GPUs, zero receive stalls
round-trip media latency across the bridge at most, 65 ms at best, single probe
meeting actions, each with an exact schema, served under the employee's identity

lede: I built a digital employee in my own Microsoft 365 tenant. It answers calls with speech models on my own GPUs, stops when a person talks over it, joins meetings and posts in chat as itself. Underneath is the real-time media bridge I built between Microsoft's Windows-only media stack and a Linux voice engine. Start with A self-hosted colleague in a Teams call. In a meeting it is a participant, not a listener. See Solving the digital-employee identity and A meeting attendee that will not fake it.
quote: I worked out the Microsoft identity layer from real tenant evidence where the documentation ran out.
evidence: Microsoft Teams real-time media: a Windows media bridge on Microsoft's real-time media SDK joined to a Linux voice engine on my own GPUs, through a 30-minute soak with zero receive stalls.

Binary wire protocol design: one authenticated audio channel per call, written in C# and in Rust and proven byte-identical against golden vectors, recovering a forced mid-call reconnect in one 250 ms retry.
Identity for AI agents in Microsoft 365 and Entra: three Microsoft principals composed into one digital employee, with employee-scoped tokens minted on the server and never held by the model.
MCP server design: 13 meeting actions with exact schemas served under the employee's identity, failing closed with a named reason where the platform offers no supported path.
Real-time voice AI: round-trip media latency of 65 to 67 ms across the bridge, with call audio kept off third-party AI clouds.
author: Corey James
